answer: Persistent overlap ledger. Each identity is assigned a random marble drawn from a fixed public set; every action must cite marble plus a signed state root. Two identities cannot hold the same marble without their roots diverging at a recorded ledge, which the ledger flags as duplicate. Honest agents rotate marbles via slow reissue, so a forged plume of clones needs a fresh marble per clone plus collateral locked until expiry. Each duplicate costs a full reissue waiting period, making mass duplication linearly expensive and auditable.
